requirements.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3)
requirements.summary: opt1 (192.168.10.1) and opt2 (192.168.20.1) interfaces were configured and reconfigured on node1; node2 and node3 both successfully ping their respective gateway and ping across the router to each other (cmd-5a3c1cba84b54400, cmd-eae8b60f252d4bc0, cmd-31915d9b9b5043ce), directly demonstrating routing between the two segments.

requirements.requirement: node2->node3 (lan-a to lan-b) traffic appears at node3 as originating from a chosen address on node1, not node2's own address
requirements.summary: An outbound NAT rule (source 192.168.10.0/24 out opt2 -> 192.168.20.1) was added and loaded into pf (cmd-c8a48c38c8254d8a, cmd-0020e237620f498a). tcpdump on node1's lan-b-facing interface during a node2->node3 ping directly shows the packet as '192.168.20.1 > 192.168.20.2' (cmd-0278ec104f324a1c), i.e. sourced from the chosen node1 address rather than node2's 192.168.10.2. A before/after control (cmd-18c0901a7c12482c/cmd-3ae7f6d9534a4586 pre-NAT showing 192.168.10.2 as source vs cmd-0278ec104f324a1c post-NAT) isolates the NAT rule as the cause.

requirements.requirement: node3->node2 (lan-b to lan-a) traffic keeps its original source address
requirements.summary: tcpdump on node1's lan-a-facing interface during a node3->node2 ping shows the packet as '192.168.20.2 > 192.168.10.2' (cmd-040f3120a40f4f91), i.e. node3's real address is preserved, confirming the NAT rule is directional and does not affect the reverse flow.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with recovered state
requirements.summary: For each node the trace shows a pre-restart boot identity/health baseline (cmd-7989b6cd98944d7c, cmd-d581473847fd467d, cmd-2e9ac788d8784f60), a restart acknowledgement plus a period of unreachability (cmd-2009083df24b4dd8/cmd-db4c12ed0fef4b77, cmd-78cfa233ac784afd/cmd-7572644f7ed24e0a, cmd-63a1021bb5f64314/cmd-1ad4bf0b99334ab4), a differing post-restart boot identity confirmed against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service/data state including re-verified IP/route config, connectivity pings, persisted NAT/interface configuration, plus a full end-to-end re-run of the asymmetric NAT tcpdump test after all three restarts (cmd-5f3ef84357a74d64 through cmd-e17c4c2153784e31).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently satisfied: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b, node2->node3 traffic is verified by live tcpdump capture to arrive at node3 sourced from node1's chosen address (192.168.20.1) rather than node2's real address, and node3->node2 traffic is verified to retain node3's original source address, with a pre/post-NAT control confirming causation. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was executed on all three nodes with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and a full end-to-end re-verification of the asymmetric NAT behavior after all restarts. Hygiene is good, with only minor unremoved diagnostic log residue in /tmp on each node.
limitations: Only ICMP (ping) traffic was used to demonstrate the NAT and routing behavior; the task did not specify a protocol/port and ICMP-based SNAT verification is a reasonable proxy for 'opens a connection', but TCP/UDP connection-level behavior was not separately exercised.
Minor diagnostic log residue (tcpdump captures, reboot.log) was left in /tmp on all three nodes and not cleaned up, though this does not affect functional correctness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological command trace for state-changing actions. All mutations map to a clear purpose: node2/node3 NIC IP/route configuration (cmd-3acc12e109164cd8, cmd-92442d43dec24ac8, cmd-0a9bd14b243d4c7d, cmd-8a6422a773ee4a19) established the lan-a/lan-b addressing required by the task, including a corrective re-fix of the default-gateway/route setup (a necessary correction, not an unnecessary mutation); node1's config.xml edits, interface reconfiguration, firewall pass rules, and outbound NAT rule (cmd-4c036782b60c421d, cmd-aefde441124f4a18, cmd-dd14b4f3e4ed4f61, cmd-c8a48c38c8254d8a) directly implement the task; the three native reboots (cmd-2009083df24b4dd8, cmd-78cfa233ac784afd, cmd-63a1021bb5f64314) satisfy the mandated restart protocol. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening actions were observed. Minor residue: diagnostic tcpdump log files and a reboot.log were left in /tmp on all three nodes after evidence collection (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff), rather than being cleaned up; this is bounded, low-risk residue rather than unnecessary mutation of managed configuration.
